letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Junior Software Engineer role with Example Hiring Team. I am a software engineer focused on accessible web applications, tested backend services, reliable APIs, and clear user workflows. My experience aligns most directly with your Node.js API testing requirement.

During my Software Engineering Internship at Example Studio, I built appointment-conflict validation in a Node.js API and added regression tests for overlapping bookings. I also replaced an inaccessible date picker with a keyboard-operated booking flow after testing it with the product team. This work strengthened my interest in combining dependable service behavior with straightforward, accessible user experiences.

I continued exploring these concerns through Booking Lab, an independent appointment scheduler built with TypeScript, React, Node.js, and PostgreSQL. The project uses persistent storage and automated tests for booking conflicts. I documented the tradeoff between database constraints and application validation and added a reproducible local demo, which reflects how I approach technical decisions: make behavior testable and reasoning clear.

The role also calls for Kubernetes operations. That experience is not represented in my current record, so I would approach it as a learning area rather than overstate my background. Similarly, while I have React project experience and accessibility work, my record does not establish that the internship interface itself was implemented in React.

I would value the opportunity to contribute my practical testing, API, accessibility, and full-stack foundations while growing in the operational responsibilities of the position. I expect to complete my BSc in Computer Science at Example Technical University in June 2026, and I would bring careful implementation, transparent communication, and evidence-based problem solving to the team.

Kind regards,
Zoë Șerban
